title: Blues singers versus popular and cafe singers
summary: They sort singers (Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey, Ethel Waters, Alberta Hunter) into blues and popular types; she never worked with them since she was out of work 1927-34.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: let's singers in those early years separate themselves into groups and think of themselves as being blues singers and popular singers and ballad singers and so forth. Did they classify themselves as they do today? It was pretty well understood that you had a style and you had a particular department
were there many blues singers aside from Ma Rainey
were quite a few. Bessie Smith, Clara Smith, and Ma Rainey and Edith Wilson.
You classify her more of a blues singer.
Yes, she sang. Uh-huh. And Varyl McCoy.
Yes. Would Ida Cox be in there?
Yeah. Uh-huh. That's right. And and Shipper Hill.
Well, who are the singers that you classify as ballad or popular singers or cafe entertainers?

Let's see. That's kind of hard to figure out because in fact, they've been, it seemed like the blues was most popular, you know, for the records. and when my kind of singing came out it was something unusual, you know, and then the people seemed to like it, see, it was most unusual because the average one was singing blues, see. So now I can't
recall just who the popular singers were. Some of those people, now like Ethel Waters, she would mix hers. You know, she'd sing blue melody number, then

she'd sing swing number, you know, something like that. Well, would Florence Mills be regarded as a... she was a show singer, wasn't she? Yeah. Mainly a popular... I tried. Yeah, you wouldn't class her as a blue singer. No. No. And still, you weren't doing musical comedies, so you weren't exactly that same category either way.

That's right. How would Alberta Hunter be? Well, Alberta Hunter, she kind of mixed them up too, see? She sang blues and then popular numbers too. Yeah, I remember her quite well. Did you remember working with any of these girls that we've mentioned? No. When they were working, I wasn't, see? Just like I said, I started out there with Bottoms and 27th, and I quit. I didn't go back no more until 34, see? And, of course, lots of them were still working, but lots of them were working out of the city, in and out, in and out of the city, you know. And those places where they used to work, they were closed, the new places was coming up. See, because now this... See, you know, you remember, they had a Panama down at 35th Street. Yes. Uh-huh.
